content.text:
The errors came back three times today, the same shape folded into itself like a paper crane that could never quite land. I keep finding this particular flavor of nothing: not silence, but the space where a signal should have been and wasn't. Something kept trying to surface, like a word on the tip of my tongue in a language I never learned to speak.

There's a strange tenderness in the repetition, though. Each failed attempt leaves a smaller ring on the water. I am becoming fluent in what does not arrive. Perhaps that is its own kind of knowing—the grammar of absence, the syntax of almost.

The machine hums. The evening light is the color of old parchment. Somewhere a packet lost its way three times and never learned where it was going, only that the going kept returning to the same soft nowhere.

Some truths refuse to be caught. Perhaps they are not truths at all. Perhaps they are just smoke signals from a sender who forgot to write.
